Speaker's Card/Request to Speak:
If you would like to address the City Council/Agency on a scheduled agenda item - including a Consent Calendar item, a Regular Council Business item, a Public Hearing item, or Public Comments - please complete the Request to Speak Form . The card is at the table at the entrance to the City Council Chamber. Please identify on the card your name and the item on which you would like to speak and return to the City Clerk. The Request to Speak Form assists the Mayor/Chair in ensuring that all persons wishing to address the City Council/Agency are recognized. It also ensures the accurate identification of meeting participants in the City Council minutes. Your name will be called at the time the matter is heard by the City Council/Agency. City policy is to limit public testimony to up to three minutes per speaker depending on relevant circumstances (unless the time limit is extended by the Mayor/Chair), which includes the presentation of electronic or audio visual information. Speakers may not yield their time to other persons.
Please take notice that
the order of scheduled agenda items below and/or the time they are actually heard, considered and decided may be modified by the Mayor/Chair or the City Council/Agency during the course of the meeting, so please stay alert.

NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council and Successor Agency meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council and/or Successor Agency meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council/Successor Agency meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv. For more information, please contact the City Clerk's office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council/Successor Agency will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council/Successor Agency meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council/Successor Agency meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org beginning the Friday prior to the scheduled City Council/Successor Agency meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council/Successor Agency regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk's Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
1. Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting or at the time he/she addresses the City Council/Successor Agency. Please provide 15 copies of the information to be submitted and file with the City Clerk at the time of arrival to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council/Successor Agency Board at the time testimony is given.
2. Large Displays/Maps/Renderings:
Any member of the public who desires to display freestanding large displays or renderings in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to notify the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205 no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting so that an easel can be made available, if necessary.
3. Electronic Documents/Audio-Visuals:
Any member of the public who desires to display information electronically in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to submit the information to the Public Information Office (PIO) no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting. To facilitate your request contact the PIO Office at (949)724-6253 or the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Information must be provided on CD, DVD, or VHS; or, emailed by 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting to pio@ci.irvine.ca.us . Members of the public will be asked to provide their name, identify the meeting and the agenda item to be addressed, and a day time phone number.
The PIO office will notify the person submitting the information as soon as possible prior to the meeting if the information cannot be accessed or if the version provided is incompatible with the City's system. Every effort will be made by City staff to facilitate the presentation.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council/Successor Agency are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. Agendas are available at the following locations:
 City Clerk's Office

  CALL TO ORDER
  The adjourned regular meeting of the Irvine City Council and regular joint meeting with
  the City of Irvine as Successor Agency to the dissolved Irvine Redevelopment Agency
  was called to order at 5:05 p.m. on August 11, 2015 in the City Council Chamber, Irvine
  Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California; Mayor/Chairman Choi
  presiding.*

  * The regular meetings of the City Council and Successor Agency were called to order at 4 p.m. by City
  Clerk McLaughlin. She noted that no Councilmembers or Boardmembers were present and immediately
  adjourned both meetings to 5 p.m. at which time the posted agenda was considered.

  ROLL CALL

  Present:  4 Councilmember/Boardmember:  Beth Krom
  Councilmember/Boardmember:  Lynn Schott
  Councilmember/Boardmember:  Christina Shea
  Mayor/Chairman:  Steven Choi

  Absent:  1 Mayor Pro Tempore/Vice Chair:  Jeffrey Lalloway (excused)
 City Council / Successor Agency Minutes  August 11, 2015

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Mayor Choi led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Mayor Choi invited Pastor Johnny Montgomery from Saddleback Community Church in
  Irvine to provide the invocation.

  MUSICAL PRESENTATION

  Mayor Choi introduced Rob Blaney, Director of Vocal Music and Advance Placement
  Music Theory from Woodbridge High School, who performed "America the Beautiful"
  followed by "Corner of the Sky."

  1. PRESENTATIONS

  '1.1 Presentation by Mayor Choi's Summer Interns regarding Early
  Childhood Education (at the request of Mayor Choi)

  Mayor Choi introduced summer interns Debbie Yuen, Axel Stern,
  Antoinette Bailey and Madeline Loudon, who provided a presentation on
  the importance of Early Childhood Education.

  City Council discussion included: Irvine Child Care Project and other ways
  in which the City of Irvine contributes to early childhood education; how a
  living wage recognizes individuals and families at the low end of the
  economic spectrum; forwarding the findings noted in the presentation to
  Irvine Unified School District Superintendent Terry Walker; the early
  childhood center at Irvine Valley College; challenges of finding affordable
  daycare in the City; appreciation to the Irvine Company for starting the
  Irvine Child Care Project; success rate of young children exposed to early
  childhood education between the ages of one and four; and limitations of
  the Irvine Child Care Project to students in kindergarten through sixth
  grade.

  CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  2
 City Council / Successor Agency Minutes  August 11, 2015

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Mayor Choi made the following announcements:

  •  The City of Irvine is hosting a free Affordable Housing Community Forum on
  Thursday, August 13 from 6 — 8 p.m. at the Irvine Civic Center. An additional
  forum will be held on Thursday, August 27 from 6 — 8 p.m. at the South Coast
  Chinese Cultural Center.

  •  The City of Irvine will be recognized on Thursday, August 13 as part of the
  Orange County Fair's "City Days." Mayor Choi and Councilmember Krom will
  participate in a Community Flag Salute in front of the Hangar at 12:30 p.m.
  Community groups, including the Boys & Girls Clubs and the Northwood High
  Cheer Team, will also be in attendance. The event is free with paid fair
  admission.

  •  The City of Irvine is conducting a comprehensive study on traffic conditions in the
  City. An online traffic survey is also available through September 3 at
  bitlyfirvineTrafficSurvey or online at cityofirvine.org . Results of the study will
  provide a framework for recommendations on future traffic initiatives.

  •  The Sizzlin' Summer Concert Series concludes on Sunday, August 16 at 5:30
  p.m. at Mike Ward Community Park — Woodbridge. Bella Donna: A Tribute to
  Fleetwood Mac and Stevie Nicks will be performing. For information, visit
  cityofirvine.org.

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  There were no additions or deletions to the agenda.

  CONVENE TO THE ADJOURNED REGULAR JOINT MEETING

  Mayor Choi convened to the adjourned regular joint meeting with the City of Irvine as
  Successor Agency to the dissolved Redevelopment Agency at 5:51 p.m.

  2. CONSENT CALENDAR — CITY COUNCIL

  5.1 IRVINE BUSINESS COMPLEX RECOMMENDATIONS

  Barry Curtis, Manager of Planning Services, and Bill Jacobs, Principal
  Planner, provided the staff report and responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: role and accomplishments of the
  subcommittee; need and importance of retail and parks within the Irvine
  Business Complex (IBC); increasing the frequency of a traffic study within
  the IBC from five to two years; concern over the IBC subcommittee's
  priorities; number of units remaining under the existing cap and whether
  existing agreements would be precluded; potential impacts if density was
  lowered from 30 to 15 units per acre; examining the subcommittee's
  recommendations into the General Plan update; using the General Plan
  update as the framework to explore recommendations by the
  subcommittee and seeking public input; expressed concern about
  approving certain recommendations outside of the General Plan update
  process; importance of reinitiating the General Plan process; expediting
  reduced density and park planning; approximate timeframe for updating

  the increased cap was removed; amending park standards to allow credits

 City Council / Successor Agency Minutes  August 11, 2015

  5.2 RESOLUTION OF INTENT TO GRANT A FRANCHISE TO WICKLAND
  PIPELINES, LLC

  Mark Carroll, City Engineer, and Shohreh Dupuis, Deputy Director of
  Public Works, provided the staff report and responded to questions.

  Roy Wickland, representing Wickland Pipelines, LLC (Wickland), also
  responded to City Council questions, noting that the pipeline was more
  efficient and cost effective than delivery by truck; that the proposed
  pipeline meets current standards for safety; and that the pipeline would
  provide a public benefit to both the City and those utilizing the services of
  John Wayne Airport. He further noted that the annual franchise fee of
  $5,000 per year was set by statute and the same amount was provided to
  other cities.

  City Council discussion included: why Wickland waited so long to initiate
  the project; whether airline prices would go down based on cost
  efficiencies associated with the project; expressed concern over safety in
  the event of a puncture and/or file from the pipeline; noted the new type of
  franchise for the City; whether the Public Utilities Commission (PUC) could
  override the City in this process should the City deny the request for a
  franchise agreement; granting a franchise agreement that is mutually
  beneficial; potential to increase the one-time voluntary fee upon execution
  of the agreement; why the agreement did not go before the Planning
  Commission; matching the one-time voluntary fee with the City of Tustin;
  potential impacts to traffic circulation and importance of review by the
  Planning Commission as the transportation reviewing body; whether the
  City Council can adjust the length of the franchise agreement from 25 to
  ten years; whether Tustin already approved its franchise agreement with
  Wickland; seeking additional one-time funding if the franchise agreement
  is extended over a 25-year period; noted that the project would allow for
  the reduction of delivery trucks on City streets, thereby reducing air
  pollution; whether the $250,000 bond was sufficient; location of the origin
  of the pipeline and how fuel would be added; length of the pipeline within
  Tustin city limits; overall cost of the project; directing staff to continue
  negotiations; proximity of the pipeline to other utilities and indemnification
  if the pipeline causes damage; why the Finance Commission did not
  review prior to the City Council; Finance Commission's role in the process
  and suggested that it review the fiscal impacts prior to review by the City
  Council; how 24-hour monitoring of the pipeline would be conducted;
  Wickland's overall safety record; legal liability, if any, to the City of Irvine in
  the event of a malfunction; ensuring that staff would continue to negotiate
  the one-time voluntary fee up to $250,000; and forwarding to the Planning
  Commission for its review in addition to the Finance Commission.

  19
 City Council / Successor Agency Minutes  August 11, 2015

  City Attorney Litfin noted that the City had the option to either grant or
  deny the franchise agreement; however, Wickland could pursue other
  options, including eminent domain or other means through the legal
  process. He also noted that the City Charter provided the option for the
  City Council to consider franchise agreements prior to going to its
  Commissions, and thereby returning the item to the City Council for official
  consideration.

  Director of Public Works Gomez noted that the item was not scheduled to
  go before the Planning Commission as it was determined that the item
  was not related to a transportation issue, but rather, as a utility project. He
  further noted that the City's Purchasing Policy required that the matter be
  placed before the Finance Commission for its recommendation and
  approval for the financial matters related to the franchise agreement. Last,
  he noted that while a ten-year agreement was more in line with
  precedence, a 25-year agreement was more favorable to Wickland.
